title: I Let the Foundry Flask Clock Catch the Mentor Who Camped My Investment

parts.text: I stepped into flask row at 8:03 a.m. and mentor Ira was already using my numbered flask. The board said: NINETY MINUTES. FLASKS STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-four, foundry steward, holding a clipboard that listed our pour. Ira shrugged. "Mentors keep the burnout." I photographed the board, the booking, and his wax in my flask. Then I asked for the flask clock. At 8:11 the foundry desk pinged why Ira's wax sat in our flask. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The foundry desk can see Ira's wax in flask row during our pour.

social.video_title: He camped my numbered investment flask — Part 1/2
social.description: Foundry, a mentor in my flask, a ninety-minute clock he posted. I logged the wax. Would you have asked for the flask clock?

parts.text: Ira called it sprue tests until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the flask still. The flask went back to my numbered rack. Ira ran a slot of their own and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: MENTORS DO NOT KEEP THE BURNOUT. I keep our pour on a labeled card. Ira brown-bags his wax. The flask finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Mentors do not keep the burnout — Part 2/2
social.description: Flask clock, numbered flask, and a second line on the board. Were sprue tests ever our pour?
